best_part: The main stage at 03:00 in the morning!! The techno was banging! The lighting was incredibly well done!
shortfalls:
- The toilets were leaking blue stuff out of them in the glamping. We are supposed to leave no trace and that looked like a serious health hazard. Also, we were told we could stay (glampers) on Sunday but the food stores closed, the toilets were left unattended (no cleaning and no water to flush). Rather say we cannot stay and then we can sort ourselves out, or that we can stay but you are on your own (to fend for yourself kind of thing ;)).
- The bars were also a nightmare - no signal so no one could buy drinks and no cash accepted. So we couldn't bring drinks from the campsites but no drinks at the bar either? In those situations (because lets face it, things can go wrong), but some flexibility needs to be implemented to keep the party alive (like accepting cash or letting people bring drinks out with them until that rectified). Without drinks, or the struggle to get, was a bit of a mood killer. 
- Glamping - not sure if I would call it glamping - the amount of spiders in the tent (eventually cuddling with us in the bed) was not so ideal. Not that I mind spiders, but I don't want them crawling on me whilst I sleep....
-  Howler was also a bit of a sh*t show - they told us we had 2 tents when we arrived, but then we only had one. This left us super confused as to if we had double-paid. The organisers at the glamping let us know that Howler was making mess ups like this. Maybe in future, you have ONE price for the tent (for two people). Not price per person per tent as you couldnt have one person in a tent. This also caused confusion.

best_part:
We enjoyed exploring the site and seeing it come to life at night. Beautiful artwork! And of course meeting new people.
We love attending Bazique!
shortfalls:
It felt a bit "commercial" compared to the previous venue in 2024 where it felt more secluded and "foresty" if that makes sense.
You want to get the sense of wandering in nature while experiencing the art, music, and people.
Seeing trucks and vehicles driving up and down all day every day did not do that for us at all and it felt like that feeling was stolen from us.
Everything was also not completely set up by Friday afternoon when we arrived, which also took away a chunk from the experience for us, it was quite disappointing.
I also feel that there could've been a similar "hidden" area or feature like the fairy garden from the previous venue... if you didn't wander, you wouldn't have found it... that was an awesome hidden surprise - Loved it!
The toilets wasn't always cleaned and didn't always feel sanitary, with often missing toilet paper too.
I also feel like everything felt very...exposed... The open areas could've been used better like the steel dragons and the large fire scull. It just gives that "wow" factor and captures your attention away from the trucks and large empty open spaces...
The bar also didn't have network for payments on Friday either, and they didn't have a backup like taking cash for example - not great! The variety of drinks could've been wider and the pricing could definitely be a bit lower too. It was quite pricey.
Food vendors was also bit pricey, good variety though.
Could do a complimentary Yoga session on Saturday and Sunday mornings..
Then most importantly, the River Stage I suppose was the Main Stage? It was a very small area, and open... Covering it for rain would be suggested. Nice features and lasers though, we enjoyed that.
fav_artist: All of Tropical Roast DJ's were amazing! And Saturday evening's DJ's really went all out!

Overall, the event just felt pretty disorganised.

The vehicle camping situation was a mess. We paid for a vehicle camping pass expecting a 5×5m spot, but both areas were already full and nobody seemed to know what was going on. Security kept sending us from one place to another, and after almost two hours we were finally taken to an open field near the BYO section. They told us to drop our gear and go park in the general car park. After more back‑and‑forth (especially since we’d paid almost R700 for the vehicle pass), they eventually let us park next to our tents. It really felt like no one was in charge.

I also felt bad for the vendors on Saturday afternoon — with no Wi‑Fi, they were struggling to take card payments.
